label: late original-phase steps and <DEL>, in sequences whose earlier tokens include l/r/i/x/s/n/a/0
explanation: Fires only during the input phase from t>=3 onward and on the <DEL> step: 87.5% of activation mass is in the original phase and 12.4% at <DEL>. It is essentially never active in the copy phase (107 of 546k steps) or at t<3. Firing rate rises with position (orig_idx 3: 2%, orig_idx 8: 50%) and with sequence length (L=9 holds 48% of mass, L<=4 almost nothing), so it looks like an accumulator that builds up over the input. Which tokens came earlier sets whether and how strongly it fires: sequences that begin with l, r or i are about 2.4x enriched, and the top examples nearly all start with two of l/r/i. The current input matters less (k, 3, m, u are about 2.2-2.6x; t and 2 are about 1.1x), and first occurrences fire more than repeats (rate 8% vs 1%). Position alone, (phase<=1)&(t>=5), gets mass recall 0.91 but precision 0.22. Requiring at least 2 earlier tokens from {l,r,i,x,s,n,a,0} lifts dev F1 to 0.40 (mass recall 0.84). Token-weighted counts gave no further gain, so the content dependence looks graded and spread across many tokens rather than crisp. Precision stays low (~0.27): many late input steps with the right history still do not fire.
